data.name: Ashes of Immortality II - Bad Blood
data.detailed_description:
Presentation



This game is the final chapter of the Ashes of Immortality series developed by Warfare Studios, already behind Vagrant Hearts, Midnight's Blessing and Valiant.

You can play the previous games here:

Description



"I told her not to get involved. I just want to go on record as saying, this is not my fault. I warned her getting involved would be bad. She never listens to me.

My name is Orlok Vladimir Dragonov, son of Konstantin Dragonov. I was born in the town of Stoker some 230 years ago. When I was 23, I was to be wed to my best friend, Elizabeth Crane. What I didn't know was that Elizabeth's sister had been turned into a vampire four years earlier. On the day of my wedding, my sister-in-law, determined to keep her sister single out of some stupid selfishness, killed and turned me. And that's my story. Kind of a downer, I guess.

Two years ago, a hunter named Simona Rinoldt freed me from a decade of captivity, imprisonment I have her father to thank for. We may have saved the world, I don't know.

Now we're here, in the Hinterlands, the land of Landis, the land of werewolves. I'd kill every human I see just for a rolled up newspaper and a poop scoop. Actually, I'd kill every human I see just for giggles, but then I'm a man of simple pleasures.

I kept telling her to stay out of other people's business. It doesn't concern us. She never listens. And this is what we get for helping people. It's never just helping. It's always something more. "What's the worst that could happen", she said.

I'll try to remember those words when they execute us for regicide."

reviews.review:
Ashes of Immortality II – Bad Blood is a narrative-focused role-playing game developed and published by Warfare Studios that continues the studio’s long-running supernatural RPG series with a story centered on loyalty, tragedy, and the burden of immortality. Built around traditional role-playing mechanics and a retro-inspired presentation style, the game favors character development and storytelling over large-scale exploration or modern cinematic spectacle. It embraces an old-school design philosophy where dialogue, world-building, and emotional investment become the driving force behind progression.

The story once again follows Orlok Vladimir Dragonov, a vampire whose existence has been shaped by loss, betrayal, and centuries of difficult choices. Throughout the series, Orlok has remained a central figure carrying emotional scars tied to his transformation and the consequences that followed. Bad Blood pushes those struggles further, placing personal relationships and unresolved conflicts at the center of the narrative. The game focuses heavily on themes involving redemption, sacrifice, identity, and the emotional cost of surviving far beyond a normal human life.

As a continuation and conclusion to an established storyline, the game places strong emphasis on narrative payoff. Longtime players who followed previous entries will likely appreciate how returning characters and unresolved events receive attention throughout the adventure. The story often feels deeply personal rather than world-ending in scope, which helps strengthen emotional moments. Relationships matter significantly, and much of the game’s appeal comes from watching characters confront consequences years in the making.

Gameplay follows a traditional structure familiar to fans of classic role-playing titles. Exploration, conversation, and turn-based combat form the foundation of progression. The systems themselves avoid unnecessary complexity, focusing instead on creating a steady rhythm where narrative advancement remains the central reward. Players move through environments, interact with characters, uncover story developments, and gradually strengthen party members through combat and progression systems.

Combat embraces simplicity rather than innovation. Encounters rely on turn-based mechanics involving skill selection, party composition, and resource management. Battles serve as an important part of progression without overshadowing the narrative focus. Players looking for highly experimental combat systems or deep mechanical customization may find the design relatively straightforward, but the simplicity allows the story to remain the primary focus throughout the experience.

Character writing represents one of the game’s strongest qualities. Warfare Studios places significant attention on dialogue and interpersonal dynamics, helping major characters feel more important than simple quest providers or supporting roles. Conversations frequently carry emotional weight, and story progression depends heavily on investment in the people surrounding Orlok’s journey. The supernatural elements help strengthen these relationships rather than replace them, ensuring emotional conflicts remain just as important as external threats.

The setting itself contributes heavily to atmosphere. Vampires, hidden dangers, ancient history, and darker fantasy themes create a world built around mystery and tension without fully shifting into horror territory. The tone remains serious for much of the adventure while occasionally allowing quieter moments to create balance. The supernatural framework gives the world personality while reinforcing the emotional struggles driving the larger story.

Visually, Ashes of Immortality II – Bad Blood adopts a retro presentation style that reflects its independent role-playing roots. Pixel-inspired environments and classic RPG design choices create familiarity for players who enjoy older role-playing experiences. The visuals may not compete technically with larger productions, but they remain consistent and effective within the game’s intended scope.

Audio design quietly supports progression without overwhelming narrative moments. Music helps establish mood during emotional scenes while maintaining atmosphere throughout exploration and combat. The soundtrack complements storytelling effectively, strengthening tension during important developments and supporting quieter moments appropriately.

The game’s pacing may divide players depending on expectations. Those searching for constant action or heavily gameplay-driven progression may occasionally find the experience slower than anticipated. Much of the enjoyment depends on engaging with conversations, character arcs, and narrative development. Players unwilling to invest in story-heavy design may struggle to connect with the game’s priorities.

Its status as part of a larger series can also create challenges for newcomers. While the broader plot remains understandable, returning players naturally gain stronger emotional impact from long-running relationships and references tied to earlier entries. The game assumes some familiarity with its universe, particularly regarding character history.

Despite those limitations, Ashes of Immortality II – Bad Blood succeeds because it remains focused on what it wants to deliver. It does not chase larger industry trends or attempt to compete through visual spectacle alone. Instead, it builds a traditional role-playing experience driven by supernatural storytelling, emotional character development, and narrative payoff.

For players who enjoy classic RPG design and story-driven fantasy adventures built around memorable characters and darker supernatural themes, Ashes of Immortality II – Bad Blood delivers a satisfying experience that values storytelling above all else while providing a fitting continuation to its established world.

Rating: 6/10
